reference.label: fibre break
reference.definition: A physical break in a fibre span that prevents optical light from traversing it.
reference.example: A cable cut between two sites leaves the downstream amplifier input dark.

reference.label: span loss increase
reference.definition: An abnormal increase in fibre-span attenuation caused by a bend, splice, stress, or similar defect.
reference.example: A tight bend adds 6 dB of span loss and reduces downstream optical margin.

reference.label: disconnected optical connector
reference.definition: An open optical connection caused by removing or unseating a connector or patch cord.
reference.example: A patch lead is unplugged at the preamplifier input, removing all incoming light.

reference.label: dirty optical connector
reference.definition: Connector contamination that introduces optical loss or reflection without fully opening the connection.
reference.example: Dust on a patch-panel connector raises pre-FEC BER by adding insertion loss.

reference.label: amplifier hard failure
reference.definition: Failure of an amplifier or its pump that leaves the amplifier with no usable optical output.
reference.example: An inline amplifier pump stops operating, making its output dark.

reference.label: amplifier gain loss
reference.definition: An amplifier degradation in which achieved gain falls below its configured set point.
reference.example: An amplifier set for 20 dB gain supplies only 17 dB.

reference.label: amplifier noise increase
reference.definition: An increase in amplifier-added noise or noise figure that reduces OSNR while signal power may remain present.
reference.example: An ageing inline amplifier adds excess ASE noise and lowers received OSNR.

reference.label: amplifier gain tilt
reference.definition: A frequency-dependent amplifier gain error that makes part of the optical band weaker than the rest.
reference.example: High-frequency channels receive 2 dB less gain than centre-band channels.

reference.label: pump ageing
reference.definition: Gradual pump deterioration that requires increasing drive current to maintain amplifier gain.
reference.example: Pump current rises steadily for several months while gain remains at 20 dB.

reference.label: transmit-laser failure
reference.definition: A hard transmitter-laser failure that removes the optical channel sent toward the remote receiver.
reference.example: A coherent transponder laser turns off and the far-end receiver loses the channel.

reference.label: card failure
reference.definition: A hard equipment-card failure that interrupts its traffic and may invalidate its monitoring.
reference.example: An OTN line card fails and stops forwarding traffic or updating counters.

reference.label: receiver degradation
reference.definition: A receiver-local sensitivity or implementation penalty that degrades decoding despite a normal optical path.
reference.example: One coherent receiver reports high pre-FEC BER while neighbouring receivers remain normal.

reference.label: transmit-laser ageing
reference.definition: Gradual transmitter-laser deterioration evidenced by an upward drift in required bias current.
reference.example: Laser bias rises from 100% to 115% of its beginning-of-life value.

reference.label: channel-margin erosion
reference.definition: A slow decline in an optical channel's available performance margin without an immediate outage.
reference.example: A channel loses 0.1 dB of margin per week while remaining in service.

reference.label: WSS attenuation drift
reference.definition: A change in a WSS channel attenuation setting or response that makes the selected channel too weak.
reference.example: A WSS intended to apply 3 dB begins applying 7 dB to one wavelength.

reference.label: WSS passband shift
reference.definition: A frequency offset of a WSS passband relative to its optical channel that creates a filtering penalty.
reference.example: The passband centre shifts away from a 193.1 THz carrier while measured power remains normal.

reference.label: WSS input-port failure
reference.definition: A hard WSS input-port failure that blocks the channels entering through that port.
reference.example: One ROADM degree input fails and blocks all wavelengths arriving on that degree.

reference.label: blocked ROADM channel path
reference.definition: A ROADM state or fault that prevents a selected channel from passing without necessarily implying input-port hardware failure.
reference.example: An add/drop route is left blocked, so one wavelength disappears beyond the node.

reference.label: differential-group-delay increase
reference.definition: An increase in polarization-mode differential group delay along a fibre path.
reference.example: A fibre event raises DGD beyond the coherent receiver's compensation margin.

reference.label: state-of-polarisation transient
reference.definition: A rapid polarization change that exceeds the coherent receiver's tracking capability.
reference.example: Movement of an aerial fibre produces a burst of polarization-related errors.

reference.label: mechanical loss disturbance
reference.definition: A brief mechanical disturbance of fibre or a patch panel that causes a transient loss excursion.
reference.example: Work on a patch panel causes a subsecond optical-power dip.

reference.label: channel-loading transient
reference.definition: A brief multiplex power disturbance caused by adding or removing optical channels.
reference.example: Adding eight wavelengths causes a short power swing across the OMS.

reference.label: protection-switch event
reference.definition: A protection selector transition that briefly interrupts an otherwise protected client service.
reference.example: Switching from the working path to protection causes a 40 ms traffic interruption.

reference.label: OTN switch-fabric failure
reference.definition: A hard failure of an OTN switch's ODU cross-connect fabric.
reference.example: A failed fabric plane disrupts every ODU routed through the switch.

reference.label: wrong ODU cross-connection
reference.definition: An OTN provisioning error that connects an ODU to an unintended destination.
reference.example: After reprovisioning, client A's ODU is connected to client B's egress.

reference.label: client-port failure
reference.definition: A hard failure of a client-facing port or its optic that interrupts the associated service.
reference.example: A failed 100GE client PHY takes its customer service down.

reference.label: instrument misreport
reference.definition: A monitoring fault in which an instrument reports an incorrect value.
reference.example: A power monitor reports -30 dBm even though an external meter shows -10 dBm.

reference.label: stale telemetry
reference.definition: A monitoring fault in which a reported value remains frozen instead of reflecting current state.
reference.example: The received-power value remains unchanged for an hour despite traffic changes.

reference.label: unspecified upstream failure
reference.definition: An unspecified failure somewhere on the incoming signal path, used when no particular component is identified.
reference.example: Loss of incoming signal is attributed to an unspecified failure on the path from the far end.

reference.label: unspecified server-layer failure
reference.definition: An unspecified failure in a server layer on which an ODU path depends.
reference.example: ODU-AIS is received following an unidentified failure in the supporting OTU layer.

reference.label: unspecified failure
reference.definition: A generic fault used when neither the failed component nor the failure mechanism is stated.
reference.example: Protection activates because of an unspecified defect on the working path.

reference.label: optical signal lost
reference.definition: No detectable light, or power below the detection threshold, is present at an optical receiver.
reference.example: A fibre cut leaves the line receiver below its loss-of-signal threshold.
synonyms: no light at the line receiver

reference.label: low channel power
reference.definition: The optical power of a particular wavelength is below its expected range.
reference.example: A channel expected at -10 dBm is measured at -17 dBm.

reference.label: normal channel power
reference.definition: Channel power is within its expected range even though another quality impairment may remain.
reference.example: A ROADM restores power to -10 dBm although passband misalignment still raises BER.

reference.label: optical supervisory channel lost
reference.definition: The OSC is absent on one fibre section and is terminated rather than propagated as the same defect.
reference.example: An inline site reports missing incoming OSC while regenerating OSC for the next span.

reference.label: optical-power excursion
reference.definition: A brief optical-power dip or swing lasting seconds or less.
reference.example: Channel loading produces a 500 ms drop in total output power.

reference.label: low OSNR
reference.definition: Optical signal-to-noise ratio is reduced by added noise or unrecovered upstream loss.
reference.example: Amplifier ASE lowers channel OSNR from 20 dB to 16 dB.

reference.label: polarisation transient
reference.definition: The received state of polarisation changes rapidly enough to challenge receiver tracking.
reference.example: A rapid SOP change produces a short burst of errored seconds.

reference.label: high differential group delay
reference.definition: Measured differential group delay is elevated enough to impair coherent reception.
reference.example: The receiver reports 40 ps DGD and an increased pre-FEC error rate.

reference.label: optical filter penalty
reference.definition: Signal-quality degradation caused by spectral narrowing or misalignment, commonly with unchanged measured power.
reference.example: A shifted WSS passband raises BER while channel power remains nominal.

reference.label: receiver-local penalty
reference.definition: A signal-quality penalty originating in one receiver and therefore not propagating through the network.
reference.example: Only one receiver shows degraded BER on an otherwise healthy channel.

reference.label: unit down
reference.definition: A failed unit carries no traffic and provides no valid monitoring values.
reference.example: A failed line card stops traffic and its performance counters cease updating.

reference.label: OTU frame alignment lost
reference.definition: A line receiver cannot recover OTU frame boundaries from the incoming signal.
reference.example: Severe OSNR degradation causes loss of OTU framing while optical light remains present.

reference.label: OTU signal degraded
reference.definition: Pre-FEC errors exceed the degradation threshold while OTU frame alignment remains intact.
reference.example: A pre-FEC BER of 2×10⁻³ causes a signal-degrade indication.

reference.label: ODU alarm indication signal
reference.definition: An ODU maintenance signal inserted or carried downstream to indicate an upstream server-layer defect.
reference.example: After OTU frame loss, ODU-AIS is inserted on every carried ODU.

reference.label: ODU misrouted
reference.definition: An ODU arrives at an unintended endpoint because of an incorrect cross-connection.
reference.example: The ODU intended for site A emerges at site B.
synonyms: ODU delivered to the wrong destination

reference.label: client service down
reference.definition: The client-facing traffic service is unavailable or interrupted in the applicable direction.
reference.example: A failed client port interrupts the associated 100GE service.

reference.label: brief client-service hit
reference.definition: A short client-service interruption, typically occurring during protection switching.
reference.example: The client experiences a 40 ms hit while traffic moves to the protection path.

reference.label: pump-current ageing indication
reference.definition: Pump drive current is rising as control compensates for pump deterioration and maintains gain.
reference.example: Current reaches 118% of beginning-of-life while traffic remains unaffected.

reference.label: laser-bias ageing indication
reference.definition: Transmit-laser bias current is rising as the laser ages.
reference.example: Laser bias increases steadily while optical output remains on target.

reference.label: declining channel margin
reference.definition: An optical channel's measured or inferred performance margin is decreasing slowly over time.
reference.example: Estimated margin declines from 4 dB to 2.5 dB over one month.

reference.label: line-wide incoming impairment
reference.definition: An impairment present on an incoming multiplex that is inherited by every wavelength routed onward.
reference.example: Excess noise on one incoming degree affects all channels switched from that degree.
synonyms: impairment affecting the whole incoming line

reference.label: condition passed unchanged
reference.definition: A signal property or impairment traverses a transparent node without correction or regeneration.
reference.example: An OSNR impairment remains on a wavelength after it passes through a ROADM.

reference.label: channels blocked
reference.definition: The channels in the applicable WSS input or route are prevented from passing.
reference.example: A failed WSS input blocks every wavelength arriving on one degree.

reference.label: comparison channels unaffected
reference.definition: Channels outside the failed component or path continue operating normally.
reference.example: Channels on other ROADM degrees remain in service after one input fails.

reference.label: optical loss-of-signal defect declared
reference.definition: A receiver asserts its optical loss-of-signal defect after input falls below the detection criterion.
reference.example: Receiver power below threshold causes the unit to declare dLOS.

reference.label: equipment defect declared
reference.definition: A unit asserts an equipment-defect indication after detecting an internal hardware fault.
reference.example: A failed card subsystem causes the unit to declare dEQ.

reference.label: traffic alarms masked by equipment fault
reference.definition: Derivative traffic alarms are suppressed or subordinated because a primary equipment alarm identifies the fault.
reference.example: A card-failure alarm remains visible while consequent framing alarms are masked.

reference.label: errored seconds produced
reference.definition: One or more monitored one-second intervals contain transmission errors.
reference.example: A polarization transient creates five errored seconds in a 15-minute bin.

reference.label: backward defect indication sent
reference.definition: A receiver transmits backward defect indication toward the source of a defective forward signal.
reference.example: On losing OTU framing, the receiver sends BDI toward the far-end transmitter.

reference.label: far-end defect reported
reference.definition: The local endpoint receives backward notification that the remote endpoint detected a defect in the locally transmitted signal.
reference.example: The local transmitter receives BDI after the remote receiver loses framing.

reference.label: local transmit-laser fault detected
reference.definition: Internal diagnostics identify a hardware fault in the current unit's transmit laser.
reference.example: Laser monitoring detects zero output and reports a transmitter fault.

reference.label: constant-gain operation
reference.definition: An amplifier control mode that adjusts pump drive to maintain configured optical gain.
reference.example: The controller raises pump current to preserve 20 dB gain after input power falls.

reference.label: weak amplifier input
reference.definition: Aggregate optical power arriving at an amplifier input is below its expected level.
reference.example: The inline amplifier receives -25 dBm instead of the expected -18 dBm.

reference.label: weak amplifier output
reference.definition: Aggregate optical power leaving an amplifier is below its expected level.
reference.example: A gain-degraded amplifier emits 4 dB below its output target.

reference.label: no amplifier input light
reference.definition: No detectable optical traffic light is present at an amplifier input.
reference.example: A preceding span cut leaves the inline amplifier input dark.

reference.label: no unit output light
reference.definition: No detectable optical traffic light leaves the unit's output.
reference.example: A failed pump leaves the amplifier output dark.

reference.label: input present but output absent
reference.definition: A unit has detectable input light but no output, distinguishing internal failure from upstream signal loss.
reference.example: A preamplifier measures valid input power but produces no output light.

reference.label: early degradation warning
reference.definition: A monitored trend reveals developing degradation before traffic is affected.
reference.example: Rising normalized pump current warns operations before gain can no longer be maintained.

reference.label: amplifier gain outside tolerance
reference.definition: Measured amplifier gain differs from its configured set point by more than the allowed tolerance.
reference.example: Measured gain of 17.5 dB against a 20 dB target exceeds the 2 dB tolerance.
synonyms: gain more than 2 dB from set point

reference.label: pump current above end-of-life threshold
reference.definition: Normalized pump drive exceeds the defined end-of-life threshold of 120% of beginning-of-life current.
reference.example: A pump requiring 123% of its initial current meets the end-of-life criterion.

reference.label: ODU trail-trace mismatch
reference.definition: The received ODU trail trace differs from the provisioned expected identifier.
reference.example: A port expecting CLIENT_A receives the trail trace CLIENT_B.

reference.label: protected service
reference.definition: A client service has distinct working and protection ODU paths available for recovery.
reference.example: A service is provisioned with disjoint working and protection routes.

reference.label: protection path selected
reference.definition: The protection selector is forwarding traffic from the protection ODU path rather than the working path.
reference.example: After a working-path fault, the selector carries traffic over the protection leg.

reference.label: protection path unavailable
reference.definition: The standby protection ODU path is defective and cannot provide an alternate route.
reference.example: Traffic remains on working while a cut makes the protection path unavailable.

reference.label: per-channel optical power
reference.definition: Optical power measured separately for each wavelength by a channel monitor.
reference.example: A ROADM channel monitor reports -9.8 dBm for the 193.1 THz channel.

reference.label: per-channel monitored OSNR
reference.definition: OSNR measured or estimated separately for each wavelength by an optical channel monitor.
reference.example: A ROADM channel monitor reports 19.5 dB OSNR for one routed wavelength.

reference.label: received optical power
reference.definition: Optical power measured at a line receiver or receive interface.
reference.example: A coherent receiver reports -13.2 dBm input power.

reference.label: received-power 15-minute history
reference.definition: Received optical-power measurements accumulated or summarized in 15-minute performance bins.
reference.example: The 10:00–10:15 bin records a mean received power of -13.1 dBm.

reference.label: line errored seconds
reference.definition: The number of line-side seconds containing errors during a 15-minute interval.
reference.example: The line interface records 12 errored seconds in the latest 15-minute bin.

reference.label: client errored seconds
reference.definition: The number of client-side seconds containing errors during a 15-minute interval.
reference.example: A client port reports seven errored seconds for the previous 15 minutes.

reference.label: receiver-estimated OSNR
reference.definition: OSNR estimated by a coherent receiver's digital signal processor rather than by an optical channel monitor.
reference.example: The coherent DSP estimates received OSNR at 17.2 dB.

reference.label: pre-FEC bit-error ratio
reference.definition: Bit-error ratio measured before forward-error correction at a coherent receiver.
reference.example: The receiver reports a pre-FEC BER of 8×10⁻⁴.

reference.label: differential group delay
reference.definition: The measured propagation-time difference between the principal polarization modes.
reference.example: The coherent DSP estimates differential group delay at 18 ps.

reference.label: polarisation change rate
reference.definition: The measured rate of change of the received signal's state of polarisation.
reference.example: The receiver reports an SOP-rate spike during aerial-fibre movement.

reference.label: amplifier input power
reference.definition: Aggregate optical power of all wavelengths measured at an amplifier input.
reference.example: An inline amplifier reports total input power of -18 dBm.
synonyms: total optical power at amplifier input

reference.label: amplifier output power
reference.definition: Aggregate optical power of all wavelengths measured at an amplifier output.
reference.example: An inline amplifier reports total output power of +2 dBm.
synonyms: total optical power at amplifier output

reference.label: normalized pump current
reference.definition: Amplifier pump drive current expressed as a percentage of its beginning-of-life value.
reference.example: The amplifier reports pump current at 118% of beginning of life.

reference.label: normalized laser bias
reference.definition: Transmitter-laser bias current expressed as a percentage of its beginning-of-life value.
reference.example: A transmitter reports laser bias at 112% of beginning of life.

reference.label: client unavailable seconds
reference.definition: The number of seconds a client service was unavailable during a 15-minute interval.
reference.example: A port records 90 unavailable seconds in the current bin.

reference.label: OSC presence status
reference.definition: A binary indication of whether the optical supervisory channel is detected at an input.
reference.example: An amplifier reports the incoming OSC as absent.

reference.label: alarm-only monitor
reference.definition: A detector used to raise alarms without exposing its underlying measured values.
reference.example: An OSC receiver reports loss status but no optical-power value.

reference.label: optical amplifier
reference.definition: An optical line amplifier that raises multiplex power without terminating individual channels.
reference.example: An EDFA amplifies the full WDM multiplex between two sites.

reference.label: booster amplifier
reference.definition: An amplifier located after a ROADM at the transmitting end of an optical multiplex section.
reference.example: A booster raises launch power before the multiplex enters the fibre span.

reference.label: inline amplifier
reference.definition: An amplifier located at an intermediate site within an optical line route.
reference.example: An inline amplifier restores multiplex power midway through a long-haul route.

reference.label: preamplifier
reference.definition: An amplifier located before a ROADM at the receiving end of an optical multiplex section.
reference.example: A preamplifier raises weak incoming line power before demultiplexing.

reference.label: coherent line interface
reference.definition: A line-side interface that transmits or receives and terminates one coherent optical channel.
reference.example: A 400G coherent line interface terminates a wavelength at the destination node.

reference.label: transponder
reference.definition: A line interface that maps a client signal to and from a line-side optical wavelength.
reference.example: A transponder carries one 400GE client over a coherent channel.

reference.label: muxponder
reference.definition: A line interface that multiplexes several lower-rate clients into a higher-rate line signal.
reference.example: A muxponder aggregates four 100GE clients onto one 400G wavelength.

reference.label: OTN line card
reference.definition: A card that terminates an OTN line signal and exposes its carried ODUs.
reference.example: An OTN line card terminates an OTU4 and presents its ODUs to the switch.

reference.label: ROADM
reference.definition: An optical node that independently adds, drops, or routes wavelength channels through WSS functions.
reference.example: A ROADM switches 193.1 THz from an incoming degree to an eastbound degree.

reference.label: OTN switch
reference.definition: An OTN device whose internal fabric cross-connects ODU containers between interfaces.
reference.example: An OTN switch connects an ingress ODU4 to a client-facing egress.

reference.label: client port
reference.definition: A client-facing interface that maps an external client signal into or out of an ODU.
reference.example: A 100GE client port maps a router connection into an ODU4.

reference.label: 10GE client port
reference.definition: A client-facing port supporting a 10 Gigabit Ethernet service interface.
reference.example: A 10GE port terminates a customer's 10 Gigabit Ethernet circuit.

reference.label: 100GE client port
reference.definition: A client-facing port supporting a 100 Gigabit Ethernet service interface.
reference.example: A 100GE port accepts a router link for OTN transport.

reference.label: 400GE client port
reference.definition: A client-facing port supporting a 400 Gigabit Ethernet service interface.
reference.example: A 400GE port connects a client router to a coherent transponder.

reference.label: OCH_LOS
reference.definition: A critical optical-channel alarm indicating loss of signal at a line receiver.
reference.example: A fibre cut removes receiver light and raises OCH_LOS.

reference.label: OTU_LOF
reference.definition: A critical alarm indicating that an OTU receiver has lost frame alignment.
reference.example: Severe OSNR degradation causes the line card to raise OTU_LOF.

reference.label: OTU_SD
reference.definition: A minor alarm indicating that pre-FEC errors exceed the OTU signal-degrade threshold.
reference.example: A dirty connector raises BER above threshold and triggers OTU_SD.

reference.label: OTU_BDI
reference.definition: A non-alarming OTU status showing that the far end reported a defect in the locally transmitted OTU.
reference.example: The remote receiver loses framing and the local transmitter reports OTU_BDI.

reference.label: EQPT_TX_FAIL
reference.definition: A critical equipment alarm indicating failure of the current unit's transmit laser.
reference.example: A transponder detects zero laser output and raises EQPT_TX_FAIL.

reference.label: EQPT_CARD_FAIL
reference.definition: A critical equipment alarm indicating an internal card hardware failure.
reference.example: An OTN line card processor fault raises EQPT_CARD_FAIL.

reference.label: AMP_INPUT_LOS
reference.definition: A critical amplifier alarm indicating absence of optical traffic light at the amplifier input.
reference.example: A span cut leaves an inline amplifier dark at its input and raises AMP_INPUT_LOS.

reference.label: OMS_LOS_P
reference.definition: A critical preamplifier alarm indicating loss of line light at the receiving end of an optical multiplex section.
reference.example: A disconnected receive patch cord causes OMS_LOS_P.

reference.label: OSC_LOS
reference.definition: A major section alarm indicating absence of the incoming optical supervisory channel.
reference.example: Excess span loss removes the OSC at an inline amplifier and raises OSC_LOS.

reference.label: AMP_FAIL
reference.definition: A critical amplifier alarm indicating that input light is present but no output is produced.
reference.example: A pump failure leaves valid amplifier input but no output and raises AMP_FAIL.

reference.label: AMP_GAIN_OOR
reference.definition: A minor amplifier alarm indicating gain outside the permitted range around its set point.
reference.example: A 20 dB amplifier measuring 17.5 dB raises AMP_GAIN_OOR.

reference.label: AMP_PUMP_EOL
reference.definition: A minor end-of-life alarm indicating excessive normalized amplifier pump current.
reference.example: Pump current reaches 123% of beginning of life and raises AMP_PUMP_EOL.

reference.label: CLIENT_SF
reference.definition: A critical client-port alarm indicating failure of the associated client service.
reference.example: A failed 100GE client port raises CLIENT_SF.

reference.label: ODU_AIS status
reference.definition: A non-alarming client-port status indicating receipt of an ODU alarm indication signal.
reference.example: A downstream client port receives ODU-AIS and reports ODU_AIS.

reference.label: ODU_BDI
reference.definition: A non-alarming ODU status indicating that the far end reports receipt of ODU-AIS.
reference.example: A remote port returns BDI after receiving AIS, causing local ODU_BDI status.

reference.label: ODU_TIM
reference.definition: A major alarm indicating that the received ODU trail trace does not match the expected source.
reference.example: A port expecting CLIENT_A receives CLIENT_B's trace and raises ODU_TIM.

reference.label: PROT_ACTIVE
reference.definition: A minor status indicating that a protection selector is using the protection ODU path.
reference.example: A working-path failure moves traffic to protection and raises PROT_ACTIVE.

reference.label: PROT_UNAVAIL
reference.definition: A minor alarm indicating that the protection ODU path is unavailable.
reference.example: A defect on the standby path raises PROT_UNAVAIL while working traffic continues.

reference.label: EQPT_PORT_FAIL
reference.definition: A critical equipment alarm indicating a hardware fault in a client port.
reference.example: A failed Ethernet PHY raises EQPT_PORT_FAIL on its port.

reference.label: OTN_FABRIC_FAIL
reference.definition: A critical alarm indicating an internal failure of an OTN switch fabric.
reference.example: A failed switching-fabric plane raises OTN_FABRIC_FAIL.

reference.label: single optical channel
reference.definition: One optical wavelength channel rather than an entire multiplex.
reference.example: WSS attenuation drift affects only the 193.1 THz channel.

reference.label: all multiplex channels
reference.definition: Every wavelength in the applicable OMS, OTS, amplifier, or incoming degree.
reference.example: An amplifier output failure interrupts all 80 carried wavelengths.
synonyms: every channel carried by the unit

reference.label: some multiplex channels
reference.definition: A proper subset of multiplexed wavelengths rather than the complete channel set.
reference.example: Gain tilt weakens the eight highest-frequency channels only.

reference.label: WSS input-port channels
reference.definition: Every channel arriving through one ROADM degree's WSS input port.
reference.example: A WSS input failure blocks all wavelengths from one degree.

reference.label: hardware unit itself
reference.definition: The managed hardware unit as an equipment object, excluding its carried traffic.
reference.example: Pump ageing is a health condition of the amplifier unit itself.

reference.label: single receiver
reference.definition: One local receiver under diagnosis, excluding neighbouring receivers and channels.
reference.example: Only this receiver reports high BER despite a normal optical path.

reference.label: all ODUs through a switch
reference.definition: Every ODU whose route traverses the affected OTN switch fabric.
reference.example: A fabric failure disrupts every ODU cross-connected through the switch.

reference.label: single ODU
reference.definition: One ODU trail or container rather than all ODUs on a link or switch.
reference.example: A wrong cross-connect misroutes one ODU4.

reference.label: client service
reference.definition: The end-user traffic service associated with a client interface and transport path.
reference.example: A failed port interrupts this customer's 100GE service.

reference.label: specific client port
reference.definition: One individual client-facing interface rather than a WSS degree input.
reference.example: EQPT_PORT_FAIL applies to one 400GE client port.

reference.label: current unit
reference.definition: The managed unit that detected the condition or raised the alarm.
reference.example: EQPT_TX_FAIL identifies a laser failure within the current unit.

reference.label: current port
reference.definition: The specific managed interface that detected or reports the condition.
reference.example: ODU_TIM is reported at the current client port.

reference.label: immediately upstream fibre span
reference.definition: The fibre section directly before the observed unit in signal direction.
reference.example: OSC_LOS is assigned to the span feeding the inline amplifier.

reference.label: preceding amplifier
reference.definition: The nearest upstream amplifier whose output feeds the span before the observed unit.
reference.example: The current site receives no light because the preceding amplifier failed.

reference.label: optical multiplex section input
reference.definition: The transmitting-side patch or connection where traffic enters an optical multiplex section.
reference.example: A disconnected patch at the OMS input removes all launched wavelengths.

reference.label: upstream ROADM channel point
reference.definition: The channel route or WSS input at the immediately preceding ROADM.
reference.example: Low power is first observed on the channel leaving the upstream ROADM.

reference.label: upstream optical path
reference.definition: Any component on the incoming optical route from the far-end transmitter to the observed receiver.
reference.example: A dirty connector somewhere on the upstream optical path causes receiver degradation.

reference.label: far-end transmitter
reference.definition: The remote line interface that transmits the optical signal received by the current unit.
reference.example: A laser failure at the far-end transmitter causes local signal loss.

reference.label: far-end receiver
reference.definition: The remote line interface that receives the optical signal transmitted by the current unit.
reference.example: The far-end receiver sends BDI after losing frame alignment.

reference.label: either service endpoint port
reference.definition: Either the local or remote client port terminating the same service.
reference.example: A client-port failure at either endpoint can interrupt the service.

reference.label: OTN switch on ODU path
reference.definition: An OTN switch or cross-connect traversed by the service's ODU trail.
reference.example: A misconnection in an intermediate OTN switch sends the ODU to the wrong egress.

reference.label: working ODU path
reference.definition: The primary ODU route used under normal protected-service operation.
reference.example: A failure on the working path triggers selection of protection.

reference.label: protection ODU path
reference.definition: The alternate ODU route reserved to protect the service.
reference.example: A cut on the protection path raises a protection-unavailable indication.

reference.label: active ODU path
reference.definition: Whichever working or protection ODU route is currently carrying service traffic.
reference.example: A defect on the active protection path interrupts the switched service.

reference.label: baseline monitoring
reference.definition: Alarm and 15-minute performance monitoring supported by every applicable transport unit.
reference.example: Every line unit reports baseline alarms and 15-minute counters.

reference.label: power-monitoring option
reference.definition: Optional capability exposing input, output, or received optical-power measurements.
reference.example: A power-monitoring-enabled amplifier reports total input and output power.

reference.label: optical-channel monitoring option
reference.definition: Optional ROADM monitoring that exposes per-channel power and OSNR.
reference.example: An OCM-equipped ROADM reports power and OSNR for each wavelength.

reference.label: advanced coherent monitoring
reference.definition: Capability exposing coherent-DSP quantities and equipment-health currents at high frequency.
reference.example: An advanced receiver reports OSNR, BER, DGD, and SOP rate each second.

reference.label: hard failure
reference.definition: An abrupt loss of required function that normally causes traffic outage.
reference.example: A transmit laser stops emitting and immediately removes the channel.

reference.label: soft degradation
reference.definition: Reduced signal or equipment quality while traffic or optical signal remains present.
reference.example: A shifted passband raises BER without removing the channel.

reference.label: incipient degradation
reference.definition: A slow trend preceding failure while traffic is not yet affected.
reference.example: Pump current rises for months while configured gain remains stable.

reference.label: transient event
reference.definition: A brief event lasting seconds or less rather than a persistent fault.
reference.example: A mechanical disturbance causes a half-second power dip.

reference.label: provisioning-associated fault
reference.definition: A fault pattern primarily associated with recent configuration or cross-connect changes.
reference.example: An ODU is misrouted immediately after a cross-connect update.

reference.label: critical severity
reference.definition: The highest listed alarm severity for major equipment or traffic loss.
reference.example: Loss of optical signal at a line receiver is classified as critical.

reference.label: major severity
reference.definition: A serious alarm severity below critical that requires operational action.
reference.example: An ODU trail-trace mismatch is classified as major.

reference.label: minor severity
reference.definition: A lower severity used for degradations, warnings, or protection states.
reference.example: A pump end-of-life warning is classified as minor.

reference.label: not alarmed
reference.definition: A reported maintenance condition or status that does not contribute active alarm severity.
reference.example: Receipt of ODU-AIS is retained as status without an active alarm severity.

reference.label: default condition handling
reference.definition: The handling rule applied when no more specific rule covers an arriving condition.
reference.example: An unclassified incoming impairment follows the unit's default handling rule.

reference.label: transparent condition forwarding
reference.definition: Forwarding an arriving condition without correcting, regenerating, or otherwise changing it.
reference.example: A transparent ROADM passes an OSNR impairment onward unchanged.

reference.label: per-channel ROADM routing
reference.definition: Independent switching of each wavelength so channels from one multiplex may follow different routes.
reference.example: A ROADM sends 193.1 THz east and 193.2 THz south.

reference.label: OTU frame-loss consequent actions
reference.definition: On OTU frame loss, insertion of ODU-AIS downstream and transmission of BDI toward the source.
reference.example: OTU_LOF causes AIS on every carried ODU and BDI toward the far-end transmitter.

reference.label: ODU-AIS forwarding
reference.definition: Transparent carriage of an incoming ODU alarm indication signal through an OTN cross-connect.
reference.example: ODU-AIS entering an OTN switch remains present on the ODU at its egress.
